newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Duhalde hits out at economy minister.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Duhalde hits out at economy minister.

text.p: A truce between Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez and Eduardo Duhalde, governor of Buenos Aires Province and presidential hopeful, has blown apart again with Duhalde writing off Fernandez as a "technocrat."

A front-page story by Clarin newspaper carried comments in which Duhalde, the number two man in the ruling Peronist Party, said: "I'm really not concerned about Roque Fernandez's opinion because he is not a Peronist."

Earlier this month, Fernandez, a former Central Bank chief who took over from Domingo Cavallo a year ago, shed his low profile and mild manners to criticize Duhalde's proposals for the creation of a new Production Ministry.
Duhalde said it was a way to promote business and foment jobs, but Fernandez saw it as an encroachment on his territory and accused Duhalde of being Peronism's "only enemy."
Duhalde, who is already profiling himself as the natural heir to President Carlos Menem when he quits the presidency in 1999, responded by calling Fernandez's "orthodox" economic ideas "out of date."
A truce ensued and Menem found a compromise by creating a Department of Small and Medium-Sized Businesses to report to the presidency and be headed by one of Menem's faithful.

But Duhalde, who is keen to distance himself from the side-effects of the free market reforms pioneered by Cavallo since 1991, the worst of which is unemployment now at 16.1 percent, appears to be calling an end to the truce.

In the comments reported Monday, he said the minister "is not a Peronist man. His opinion on the economy may have some value, but as far as the politics of the Peronist Party are concerned, their value is relative."
Asked if he considered Fernandez to be a "technocrat" just like his predecessor Cavallo, Duhalde replied:
"I don't consider him a technocrat -- he is a technocrat. An outstanding one, but a technocrat at the end of the day."
